findings.title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer instead of a User record
findings.body: ActiveRecord's `CollectionProxy#delete` expects record objects, not integer IDs. `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer will not remove the user from the group — it will either raise an error or silently do nothing depending on the Rails version. The correct approach is to find the user first (e.g., `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))`) or use `group.users.where(id: user_id).destroy_all`.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is evenly divisible by limit
findings.body: The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` returns one extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit. For example, with 100 users and limit 50, it returns 3 instead of 2. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This also causes `showingLast` to be wrong, allowing the user to navigate to an empty page.

findings.title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method
findings.body: The test uses `xhr :put, :remove_member` but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. A PUT request to this route will result in a routing error (404), not the expected 422. The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` to match the route definition. The second test in the same context correctly uses `:delete`.

findings.title: add_members does not strip whitespace from usernames after splitting
findings.body: When the client sends usernames like "user1, user2" (with spaces after commas, which is common from autocomplete UIs), `usernames.split(",")` produces `["user1", " user2"]`. The leading space in `" user2"` will cause `User.find_by_username` to fail, silently skipping that user. Each username should be stripped: `username.strip`.

findings.title: create action ignores alias_level sent by the frontend
findings.body: The frontend's `asJSON()` method includes `alias_level` in the payload for both create and save operations. However, the server-side `create` action only sets `name` and `visible`, ignoring `alias_level`. If a user sets an alias level before creating a new group, that setting will be silently lost. The `update` action does handle `alias_level`, making this inconsistent.

findings.title: No upper bound on limit parameter allows unbounded queries
findings.body: The `members` action accepts `params[:limit]` without any upper bound validation. A client can request `limit=999999999`, causing the database to attempt loading an enormous result set. This is a denial-of-service vector. The limit should be clamped to a reasonable maximum (e.g., 1000).

findings.title: next action can set offset equal to user_count, producing an empty page
findings.body: In the `next` action, `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))` can produce an offset equal to `user_count` (e.g., offset=50, limit=50, user_count=100 → new offset=100). This offset is then clamped to `user_count` in `findMembers` and sent to the server, which will return zero members. The offset should be capped at `user_count - limit` or the `showingLast` guard should prevent this case (which it fails to do due to the `totalPages` bug).
